title: Content: routine & block library (SPEC §7)
description:
Curated workout content on top of the MVP schema — all pure data files designed WITH the owner; deliberately no in-app editor UI (SPEC §2). Children: GIF fetch tooling + quota ledger, warm-up/cooldown blocks, two dumbbell strength routines, physio rehab blocks (hard-gated on the MVP phone test ft-mvp-ow6.11), and 40+ min sessions composed from blocks.

## Success Criteria

- Physio blocks carry citations from reputable sources.
- All child beads closed.

title: GIF fetch script + committed quota ledger (SPEC §6.10)
description:
node scripts/fetch-gifs.mjs <exerciseId...> (SPEC §6.10, §4): reads WORKOUTX_KEY from env (never committed — public repo), downloads missing GIFs to data/gifs/, skips files already present, paces under 30 req/min, records the X-Quota-Remaining response header, and appends {date, ids, calls, quotaRemaining} to a committed ledger (data/quota-ledger.json). Treat 503 'watermarked GIF unavailable' (known: ids 5202, 5204) as skip-and-report so a substitute can be chosen — never retry a 503 into the quota. ~330 of 500 monthly calls remain as of 2026-08-10; batch fetches per design session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Running twice for the same ids costs zero API calls the second time.
- Ledger matches the API's reported quota drift.
- A 503 id is skipped with a clear report and no retries.
acceptance_criteria: second run for same ids costs zero calls; ledger matches API quota drift; 503 ids skip with report, no retry
notes: The approved useful-first visual path is now the private clip-pack graph. Keep this quota-aware WorkoutX GIF fetcher for future catalog gaps only; it is no longer the next delivery priority.

title: Implement four integrated routines (v2) as app data — W1-W4 super workouts
description:
Implement the four integrated "super workout" routines as installable app data so the owner can test them on his phone.

CANONICAL SPEC: docs/research/draft-routines-v2.md — exact per-interval exercise lists, sides, coach cues, RPE targets, and global safety rules for W1 "Iron Roots" (30×40/20), W2 "Silk Coils" (30×40/20), W3 "Dragon Longform" (45×40/20), W4 "Crane Longform" (45×40/20). Do not re-derive intervals from anywhere else; v2 already incorporates the oracle design review (docs/research/oracle-routine-review.md) over the five-source evidence base (docs/research/synthesis.md; profile in docs/research/interview.md).

Scope:
1. Map every v2 exercise to the WorkoutX catalog (data/exercises/catalog_full.json) by name/target; record the mapping (exerciseId or none) per interval.
2. Media (OWNER PIVOT 2026-08-10): primary visual = looping video clip slices — sources from ft-content-e0q.8 (clip-sources map), produced by ft-content-e0q.9 (make-clips pipeline), rendered via ft-mvp-ow6.16 (video cards). Fallback chain per interval: clip -> GIF (reuse the 27 in data/gifs/, fetch missing via ft-content-e0q.1 within quota) -> text card with the coach cue as body (established for MadFit interval 2); a text card is a deliberate choice, not a failure. Do not commit clips lacking redistribution-safe licenses until the owner resolves the public-repo licensing question (see e0q.8).
3. Write the four routine JSONs per data/SCHEMA.md (blocks where reuse is natural — e.g. the shared warm-up ramp and rehab-spine stations — inline intervals otherwise). Encode coachNotes: tempo, RPE target, and the safety cues from v2's global rules (toe-safe regression, planted feet, neutral grip, calf 3-1-3).
4. Timer semantics: sessions must run exactly 30:00/45:00 — the final 20 s rest is kept (v2 header; verify engine behavior, fix or file if it stops after last work interval).
5. Register all four in the picker (data/content-index.json or current mechanism) — zero app-code changes expected; if code changes ARE needed, that is a schema/picker bug to file separately.
6. Validate: node scripts/validate.mjs over all routine files passes; every interval renders either a GIF or a text card.

Out of scope: the habit-anchored Achilles dosing card (docs, not app data); the dedicated clinic routine (future); qigong (skipped by owner decision 2026-08-10).

Done means: all four routines validate, appear in the picker, and are runnable end-to-end on the deployed PWA so the owner can try them ASAP.
acceptance_criteria: all four routines validate, appear in the picker with zero app-code changes, every interval shows a GIF or deliberate text card with cues, and each runs exactly 30:00/45:00 end-to-end on the deployed PWA

title: Slice MadFit 07c6wlJh89U into the first 30-exercise private clip pack
description:
## Background
The current source workout is MadFit's 30 MIN FULL BODY HIIT with weights (video ID 07c6wlJh89U). Its 30 named 40-second intervals already exist in data/blocks/madfit-30min-hiit.json, but several WorkoutX GIFs are weak, misleading, or text-only. This bead creates the first complete private exercise clip database from the exact coached source before searching other channels.

## Technical Approach
Work in a private media directory outside the Git checkout. Use yt-dlp to acquire the source once at no more than 720p, with metadata/subtitles retained privately for analysis. For each of the 30 current interval display names:
1. locate the exercise work window;
2. select a clean 1-3-repetition loop showing the full movement, side and equipment;
3. slice a short reference clip, normally 3-8 seconds;
4. remove the audio stream with ffmpeg -an, encode phone-compatible H.264 MP4/yuv420p with faststart, and create a poster;
5. verify zero audio streams with ffprobe;
6. name/map the clip by stable movementId and the current interval displayName.

Add dependency-free repository tooling under scripts/media/ to build and validate packs while keeping sources/outputs outside Git. Build a metadata clip catalogue containing movementId, exact displayName, source video ID/URL, source start/end, loop range, side, equipment, viewpoint, framing, mirroring rule, quality/form notes, prospective mocap range, duration, dimensions, file size and hash. The metadata catalogue may be committed; source video and derived clips may not.

The deliverable is 30 interval records and 30 usable loop records, including distinct right/left or side-1/side-2 records where the workout does so. Compound intervals remain named as the workout names them and show the compound sequence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The private reference-v1 pack contains one correctly named, usable loop and poster for every one of the 30 MadFit interval names.
- Each loop shows at least one complete repetition or complete compound sequence, correct side/equipment, full body or relevant contact points, and no obvious seam, long hold, or crop.
- ffprobe reports zero audio streams for every released loop; a scripted validation fails on any audio-bearing, missing, duplicate, or unmapped clip.
- The clip catalogue records exact timestamps and analysis sufficient to revisit the source or attempt wireframe mocap later.
- The pack imports through the FitTimer media runtime and works offline; at minimum the former weak/text intervals 2, 16, 19 and 27 visibly improve.
- Source/derived media remain outside Git and public Pages; repeated tooling runs are idempotent and do not redownload completed sources unnecessarily.

## Test Plan
Unit-test catalogue/manifest generation and validation with small synthetic fixtures. Run the built-in ffprobe audit across the completed private pack, validate exact coverage against data/blocks/madfit-30min-hiit.json, import it into the PWA, and complete an offline phone smoke pass with background music.

## Considerations
This bead covers only video 07c6wlJh89U. Do not search Pamela Reif, Caroline Girvan, Heather Robertson, Sydney Cummings, Growingannanas or other sources here; those searches will be scoped from approved routine gaps after this first database proves the format.
acceptance_criteria: All 30 current MadFit interval names have correctly mapped private silent loops and posters; ffprobe proves zero audio streams; catalogue contains timestamps/form/framing/mocap metadata; pack imports and runs offline; no source or clip media enters Git or Pages.

title: Clip source map: per-exercise video sources for v2 routines (data/media/clip-sources.json)
description:
Research and produce the per-exercise video source map for the v2 routines: data/media/clip-sources.json.

OWNER DECISION 2026-08-10: exercise visuals move from WorkoutX GIFs to small looping video-clip slices; GIFs and text cards remain the fallback chain.

For every unique exercise in docs/research/draft-routines-v2.md (~80 across W1-W4), find the best video demonstration and record: {exercise, sourceUrl, startTime, endTime (target 2-6 s loopable segment showing 1-2 clean reps), cropHint?, license, fallback: gifId | textCard}. An explicit "no good source -> fallback" entry is a valid result, not a gap.

Source priority: (1) openly licensed / CC content (e.g. CC-BY exercise libraries, institutional physio channels that permit reuse); (2) the already-archived MadFit video (data/youtube/) for exercises it demonstrates; (3) other YouTube demonstrations — flagged, see licensing note. Record the license/permission status for EVERY entry; entries without a redistribution-safe license must be marked redistributable:false.

LICENSING CONSTRAINT (unresolved, owner to decide before clips are committed): this repo is PUBLIC. Slicing third-party YouTube videos into clips committed to a public repo is copyright-relevant in a way the watermarked free-tier GIFs already skirt. The mapping file itself (URLs + timestamps) is safe to commit; the produced clips may need to stay untracked/locally-hosted, the repo may need to go private, or sources must be restricted to permissive licenses. Surface the totals (how many exercises have redistribution-safe sources) so the owner can decide with real numbers.
acceptance_criteria: clip-sources.json covers every unique v2 exercise with either a timed loopable source (license recorded) or an explicit gif/text fallback; redistribution-safe count reported to owner

title: Clip production pipeline: yt-dlp + ffmpeg slice/loop/compress (scripts/make-clips.mjs)
description:
Build the clip production pipeline: scripts/make-clips.mjs (node orchestrating yt-dlp + ffmpeg, both available on the 3090; no npm dependencies per repo policy — shell out).

Reads data/media/clip-sources.json entries and produces data/clips/<slug>.mp4:
- Download source segment (yt-dlp --download-sections or full + slice), cut startTime..endTime.
- Loop-friendly output: short 2-6 s segment; optional crossfade or reverse-append ("boomerang") flag per entry for seamless looping when the movement is not naturally cyclic.
- Uniform spec: H.264 mp4 (universal iOS/Android playback), muted (audio stream stripped), ~480px on the long edge, target <=1.5 MB per clip, faststart flag for instant playback.
- Idempotent: skips clips already present; re-running for the same mapping costs nothing.
- Caches source downloads outside the repo (scratch dir) so re-slicing does not re-download.
- Respects redistributable:false entries with a --local-only mode note in output (clips still produced for personal use; committing them is the owner's licensing call, see clip-sources bead).

Landable independently of the full source map: acceptance uses 2-3 sample entries (e.g. from the archived MadFit video in data/youtube/).
acceptance_criteria: sample mapping entries produce muted H.264 loops <=1.5 MB with faststart; second run for same entries does no work and no re-download

title: Routine & block schema + validator; convert MadFit JSON (SPEC §6.1)
description:
The contract everything else depends on — engine, picker, and all future content. Block = named, reusable ordered list of intervals {exerciseId, displayName, gif, workSeconds, restSeconds, side?, coachNote?}. Routine = metadata {title, equipment, estDuration} + ordered list of block refs and/or inline intervals. Must support per-side exercises, combo intervals (two movements alternated in one interval — MadFit #12/#22/#23), and blocks shared across routines. Deliverables: data/SCHEMA.md documenting every field; a dependency-free validator (node scripts/validate.mjs data/routines/*.json); convert data/routines/madfit-30min-hiit.json (interim shape — see its notes field) to the final schema as the reference example.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Validator passes on the converted MadFit routine and rejects committed bad fixtures (missing gif ref, zero/negative seconds, unknown block ref, invalid side) — keep the fixtures in the repo as the validator's test suite.
- Schema expresses per-side exercises, combo intervals, and cross-routine block reuse.
- data/SCHEMA.md documents every field, its optionality, and units.
acceptance_criteria: validator passes on converted MadFit routine and rejects committed bad fixtures; schema covers per-side, combo, and cross-routine block reuse; SCHEMA.md complete

title: Personal settings: cue, voice, and visual preferences
description:
## Background
FitTimer currently has no settings store or settings UI. WebAudio tones are hard-coded, voice is planned but not implemented, and the selected visual pack does not yet exist. This is a one-user personal app, so the goal is a small dependable preference surface rather than an account or profile system.

## Technical Approach
Add a versioned settings module backed by one localStorage key. Validate every load, use stable versioned IDs, and fall back to defaults for missing, malformed, or unknown values without blocking startup. Add a compact home-screen settings panel for:
- cues: pack, enabled, master volume, countdown, halfway;
- voice: pack, enabled, volume, exercise/side/next announcements;
- visuals: selected media-pack ID and reduced motion.
Apply the cue controls to AudioCuePlayer. Persist voice and visual choices for their owning features to consume. Ship one synth cue pack initially; pack selection is an extensibility contract, not a marketplace.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Settings persist across reload and service-worker cache updates.
- Malformed JSON and unknown IDs fall back to documented defaults with no console error or broken workout.
- Cue enable/volume/countdown/halfway controls affect exactly the intended WebAudio events.
- Voice and visual selections are stored as stable IDs and exposed through the settings API.
- The settings panel is usable at 390x844 and does not crowd the workout controls.

## Test Plan
Add dependency-free unit tests for load/save/migration/default fallback and AudioCuePlayer filtering/volume. Run node --test, scripts/check-pwa.mjs, and a 390x844 browser pass covering edit, reload, and corrupt-storage recovery.

## Considerations
Do not store media blobs or workout history in the settings key. Missing packs must degrade safely to built-in defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Versioned cue/voice/visual preferences persist; malformed or unknown settings fail safely; cue enable, volume, countdown, and halfway controls work; 390x844 browser flow and unit tests pass.

title: Media-pack contract: stable movement IDs and pluggable visuals
description:
## Background
Schema v1 binds each movement directly to a data/gifs path, so the exercise meaning and its current rendering cannot vary independently. FitTimer needs stable movement identities that can resolve through the built-in GIFs today and private silent-video packs later.

## Technical Approach
Introduce schemaVersion 2 for movement visuals. Each movement carries a stable movementId plus displayName and optional exerciseId/textOnly semantics. Define a small versioned media-pack manifest mapping movementId to one or more render assets: silent video, animated WebP or GIF, poster, safe-framing metadata, anatomical side, and an explicit mirroring policy. Generate a built-in gif-v1 manifest from the current MadFit mappings and migrate the current block/routine without visual change. Update SCHEMA.md, validator, fixtures, content URL collection, and runtime resolution. A missing pack entry must fall back to poster/text rather than blank UI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All current content validates as schemaVersion 2 and the MadFit workout looks unchanged with gif-v1.
- Validator rejects missing movementId, invalid pack records, and uncovered referenced movement IDs.
- Adding or changing a visual for an existing movement requires only a media-pack data change, not app code or routine changes.
- Offline caching resolves only the selected pack assets referenced by installed routines.
- Framing and mirroring rules are explicit data, not filename or pixel heuristics.

## Test Plan
Add focused validator fixtures for the new failure modes, run scripts/test-validator.mjs, node --test, scripts/check-pwa.mjs, and a browser offline-reload workout using gif-v1.

## Considerations
This is a direct early-project schema migration; do not add v1 compatibility wrappers. Keep the manifest intentionally small and local-first.
acceptance_criteria: Schema v2 separates stable movement IDs from visual files; current MadFit content migrates with unchanged gif-v1 rendering; validator covers missing/invalid media mappings; selected-pack offline caching and fallback pass.

title: Private clip-pack import, silent video playback, and offline fallback
description:
## Background
The public PWA must be able to use a private exercise-reference pack without committing or serving source clips from GitHub Pages. The current renderer supports only img or text cards. The useful-first replacement is a short, silent, looping video reference.

## Technical Approach
Add a local media-pack import flow for a manifest plus its files. Persist the selected manifest metadata and media blobs locally using browser storage suitable for offline playback; localStorage stores only the selected pack ID. Resolve assets through the media-pack contract. Render video with muted, playsinline, loop, autoplay and poster; fall back video -> animated WebP/GIF -> poster -> text. Reduced-motion mode uses posters only. Keep object containment and safe framing so bodies and equipment are never cropped. Imported packs must survive reload and airplane mode and be removable without breaking routines.

All generated clip files must have the audio stream removed, not merely volume muted. Runtime video remains muted defensively. Do not use Media Session or an audio element; cues and voice remain WebAudio.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A private test pack can be imported on phone, selected, played through a workout, reloaded, and used in airplane mode.
- Missing, deleted, corrupt, or foreign-version packs fall back to gif-v1/poster/text with no blank stage.
- Videos loop silently, remain fully framed, and do not autoplay when reduced motion is enabled.
- With background music playing, a video-bearing workout does not pause or duck music on the owner's target phone; this on-device evidence is required to close.
- No private media appears in Git status or the public Pages asset list.

## Test Plan
Unit-test deterministic media selection/fallback. Extend PWA checks to enforce muted and playsInline video creation plus the existing no-audio/no-Media-Session policy. Run a desktop import/offline browser pass and record the real-phone background-music result in the close evidence.

## Considerations
Support one selected private pack plus the built-in fallback. Do not build pack discovery, sharing, accounts, or a marketplace.
acceptance_criteria: Private pack import survives reload and airplane mode; silent playsinline loops use safe framing and fallback cleanly; reduced motion uses posters; real-phone background music is not paused or ducked; no private media enters Git or Pages.

title: Workout screen video-loop rendering with gif/text fallback chain
description:
Workout screen renders looping video clips as the primary exercise visual, with fallback chain: video clip -> GIF -> text card (text-card path already exists for MadFit interval 2).

Requirements:
- <video muted autoplay loop playsinline preload> pattern; no controls, no Media Session registration, no audio track. THE CORE INVARIANT APPLIES: must not pause or duck the user's background music. Muted inline video normally does not take audio focus, but this MUST be verified on real Android Chrome and real iOS Safari with Spotify playing — that verification is part of this bead's acceptance, not a separate task.
- iOS autoplay: muted + playsinline is the documented requirement; ensure playback resumes after tab background/foreground (re-play on visibilitychange alongside the existing wake-lock re-acquire).
- Service worker precaches clips referenced by installed routines exactly like GIFs today (schema/media field addition if needed — coordinate with data/SCHEMA.md; adding a clip must require zero app-code changes).
- Rest-interval "next up" preview shows the next exercise's clip.
- Memory: only the current (and next) clip mounted; long 45-interval sessions must not accumulate video elements.

Acceptance: on the deployed PWA with Spotify playing, a routine whose intervals mix clip/GIF/text-card media runs a full session offline (after one online visit) with music never interrupted, clips looping smoothly, and correct fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: mixed-media routine runs a full offline session on the deployed PWA with Spotify playing on real Android and iOS: music never pauses/ducks, clips loop, fallbacks render

title: PWA shell: offline via service worker, installable (SPEC §6.2)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Full session runs in airplane mode after one online visit.
- Add-to-Home-Screen works on Android Chrome and iOS Safari.
- Bumping the SW cache version picks up changed routine files without a manual cache clear.
acceptance_criteria: airplane-mode session works after one online visit; A2HS on Android + iOS; SW version bump refreshes cached routines

Remaining acceptance: Android and iOS Add-to-Home-Screen plus a complete real-device airplane-mode session.

title: Interval engine: timestamp-anchored state machine (SPEC §6.3)
description:
Pure JS state machine (idle/work/rest/paused/done) as a standalone module with no DOM access (SPEC §6.3). Timing is timestamp-anchored: compute remaining time from clock deltas, never accumulate setInterval ticks. Controls: pause/resume, skip forward/back one interval, restart. Emits tick, intervalStart, intervalEnd, halfway, countdown321; UI and audio are subscribers only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unit tests (node --test, injected fake clock, zero deps) cover: every state transition, pause/resume across a work→rest boundary, skip at first/last interval, restart, and recovery after a simulated 10s stall.
- A 30-interval run finishes within 1s of wall clock.
- Skip/pause/resume never desync display state from engine state.
acceptance_criteria: node --test suite passes (fake clock: transitions, boundary pause/resume, edge skips, 10s stall); 30-interval run within 1s of wall clock
close_reason: Delivered pure timestamp-anchored idle/work/rest/paused/done engine with pause/resume, skip both directions, restart, and required events. node --test passes fake-clock transitions, boundary pause/resume, edge skips, restart, 10s stall recovery, cue timing, and 30-minute wall-clock anchoring; UBS exits 0 after triage.

title: Workout screen UI + navigation: Previous / End Workout / completion (SPEC §6.4)
description:
## Background
The phone-first workout screen is implemented and its GIF cropping defect is fixed. Navigation semantics remain confusing: Back calls engine.skipBack(), silently does nothing during interval 1, and changes meaning to Home only after completion. There is no deliberate way to end an active workout.

## Technical Approach
Preserve the existing timer engine. Rename Back to Previous and visibly disable it throughout interval 1. Add an explicit End Workout control that pauses and opens an in-app confirmation; Keep Going resumes from the paused timestamp, while End returns home and stops the animation loop. On completion, show explicit Home and Restart actions rather than repurposing unrelated controls. Keep Previous/Next/Pause sized and placed for sweaty-thumb use. Retain the next-up rest preview, text-only fallback, safe media containment, progress, and responsive dark layout.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Previous is visibly disabled during interval 1 work/rest and works from interval 2 onward.
- End Workout always requires confirmation; cancelling resumes accurately and confirming returns home with no running timer/animation.
- Completion presents explicit Home and Restart actions and both work.
- The existing rest preview, text-only interval, safe framing and full-session phone ergonomics remain correct.
- A 390x844 browser flow and the eventual real-phone workout reveal no navigation mis-taps.

## Test Plan
Extend the browser/E2E pass for interval-1 disabled state, Previous from interval 2, End/cancel/confirm, Home and Restart after completion. Run node --test and scripts/check-pwa.mjs.

## Considerations
Do not overload Home as an active-workout skip. History/partial-completion recording remains owned by ft-mvp-ow6.12.
acceptance_criteria: Previous disabled at interval 1 and functional later; confirmed End returns home and cancel resumes accurately; completion has working Home/Restart; existing phone UI behavior remains correct.
notes: Workout UI is implemented. GIF clipping defect found during visual QA: intrinsic square grid items rendered 348px tall inside a 254px stage despite object-fit: contain. Fixed by constraining the grid row with minmax(0, 1fr) and allowing image min-height: 0. Playwright at 390x844 and 1024x900 confirms complete single and two-GIF interval renders with zero page/console errors. Bead remains open pending a full real-phone session/mis-tap check.

title: Audio cues via WebAudio that don't kill background music (SPEC §6.5)
description:
WebAudio-synthesized beeps only: 3-2-1 countdown, distinct work-start and rest-start tones, optional halfway tick (SPEC §6.5). NEVER an <audio> element or Media Session use — those pause/duck the user's Spotify/YT Music, and playing over the user's own music is this app's core differentiator. Create/resume the AudioContext on the Start tap (autoplay policy).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Cues audible over playing Spotify on real Android Chrome AND real iOS Safari; music never pauses or ducks.
- Every engine cue event (countdown321, intervalStart work/rest, halfway) produces its distinct sound through a full session.
acceptance_criteria: cues audible over Spotify on real Android Chrome and iOS Safari with zero music pause/duck; all engine cue events sound correctly
notes: Implemented WebAudio-only synthesized cues for intervalStart, intervalEnd, halfway, and countdown321. AudioContext is created/resumed from the Start gesture; stale catch-up events are suppressed. Verified with 5 unit tests, full 15-test suite, PWA policy checks forbidding <audio>/Media Session, and a real Chromium browser unlock/start check at 390x844 with no page errors. Acceptance remains open pending Spotify mixing verification on real Android Chrome and iOS Safari through a full session.

title: Voice: pre-rendered FrankenTTS clips + SpeechSynthesis fallback (SPEC §6.6)
description:
DECIDED (SPEC §6.6): pre-render every phrase with FrankenTTS (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_tts — Rust Qwen3-TTS reimplementation, MIT code + Apache-2.0 weights) at CONTENT-BUILD time on the owner's 3090 box, ship small audio clips with the PWA, play via WebAudio. On-phone runtime FrankenTTS was evaluated and REJECTED: ~2 GB model, several GB RAM, desktop-only, 0.31x real time in WASM. The vocabulary is tiny and fixed (exercise names, 'go', 'rest', digits, 'left'/'right'), so clips are cheap. Deliverable includes a scripts/ tool that renders a routine's phrase list to clips. Fallback: browser SpeechSynthesis for any phrase lacking a clip — iOS requires a user-gesture unlock, so initialize speech on the Start tap. Behavior: announce next exercise (and side) during rest; 'go'/'rest' at boundaries; toggleable; queued so speech never overlaps the 3-2-1 beeps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Eyes-free MadFit session possible: every interval announced in time, sides included.
- All MadFit phrases have pre-rendered clips; the SpeechSynthesis fallback demonstrably speaks a deliberately clip-less phrase on iOS after the Start-tap unlock.
- Speech never overlaps countdown beeps.
acceptance_criteria: eyes-free session works; all MadFit phrases pre-rendered; fallback speaks clip-less phrases on iOS post-unlock; speech never overlaps beeps
notes: Consume voice pack/enabled/volume/announcement preferences from ft-mvp-ow6.13; do not create a second settings store or UI.

title: Wake lock + ergonomics (SPEC §6.7)
description:
Screen Wake Lock API with re-acquire on visibilitychange (SPEC §6.7; iOS needs >= 16.4). The engine's timestamp anchoring must keep the timer honest through brief backgrounding — verify on-device, don't assume.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Screen stays on through a full 30-min session on the owner's phone.
- Backgrounding the tab for 10s and returning shows correct remaining time and interval, and the wake lock is re-acquired.
acceptance_criteria: screen stays on for a full 30-min session; 10s backgrounding preserves correct time/interval and re-acquires the lock

title: Home screen routine picker, zero-code routine add (SPEC §6.8)
description:
Home screen lists routines from data/routines/ with title, duration, equipment, exercise count; tap to start (SPEC §6.8). Static hosting has no directory listing, so the picker needs a precached routine index as DATA (e.g. data/routines/index.json, kept by the ft-mvp-ow6.1 validator or by hand per SCHEMA.md) — dropping in a routine file must never require touching app code. Leave a layout slot for history/streaks (ft-mvp-ow6.12); do not build it yet.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adding a routine JSON (+ its index entry) makes it appear and run with zero app-code changes.
- Displayed metadata matches the routine file's contents.
acceptance_criteria: new routine JSON + index entry appears and runs with zero app-code changes; displayed metadata matches file
